All 17 node + 28 python tests pass; zero approximation or per-side reimplementation exists - protocol.mjs dispatches into normalizeText/checkNormalizedView/alignPage literally.

criteria.criterion: missing Node yields clear capability error, not fallback algorithm
criteria.detail: CapabilityErrorTests covers all absence modes: PATH manipulated to an empty dir (CompareBridge() -> BridgeCapabilityError reason='capability'), nonexistent explicit node path, missing entrypoint file, injected spawn raising FileNotFoundError (ENOENT) and PermissionError. test_no_fallback_path_exists asserts the module surface carries no normalize/align implementation to degrade to - comparison exists only as a bridge call, so a missing runtime is a typed failure, never a divergent Python approximation.

The selectors pump byte-counts every stdout chunk; the instant the count exceeds max_response_bytes it SIGKILLs the child's whole process group and raises BridgeError('output_limit') - never a truncated answer. BoundedIoTests: a real comparison whose JSON legitimately exceeds a 512-byte cap yields output_limit; a real 16 MiB stdout flood from an injected runaway child is killed and bounded; stderr flood (>1 MiB) is likewise output_limit; request over cap refuses before spawn (spawned list stays empty). The entrypoint additionally self-bounds stdin (32 MiB -> SIZE ok:false, never a partial read) and its own response (64 MiB -> RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE).

argv is always exactly [resolved node, repo entrypoint] with shell=False and a minimal env (locale + private TMPDIR scratch; no PATH, no NODE_OPTIONS) - there is no argv/env construction path for request or report data to reach. FixedArgvTests records the spawn argv across hostile inputs: '--input-type=module', '$(rm -rf /) && `--eval process.exit(9)`', '"; exec("/bin/sh") #', 'NODE_OPTIONS=--require=evil' are normalized as inert text while argv stays fixed; smuggled page fields ('profile', 'exec') are rejected by the closed schema (remote_field) with argv unchanged. The node suite independently asserts closed-envelope FIELD rejection and pure dispatch.

comparatorIdentity() rides EVERY response envelope (describe, normalize, align and even error replies): package @inkflip/compare, bridge_version 1.0.0, protocol inkflip-compare-bridge v1, normalization scalar-whitespace-v1, alignment region-match-v1, score_semantics algorithm_diagnostics_not_probability, node version and platform. limitations: Verified on macOS arm64 only; POSIX-only by design (process-group kill, start_new_session). Linux verification is a coordinator dispatch.
Requires a Node with direct .ts type stripping (v26 here); older runtimes exit nonzero and surface as typed capability/child failures, never results.

The bridge defends the invocation boundary (fixed argv/env, bounded streams, group kill); it is not a sandbox for hostile entrypoint code - supervised containers remain the hardened route for untrusted corpora.
T31 ships the bridge and parity proof only; wiring into report/manifest writers is a later task's scope.
